# v4

This folder is the Infisical 2.0 component source of truth. It is incubating. Product code must not import it. The only UI importer outside this folder is `src/pages/design-system`. Dedicated generation and introspection scripts may read the typed metadata; product code remains fenced from all v4 imports.

For the contribution workflow, read [Infisical UI](skills/infisical-ui/SKILL.md). Its [canonical rules](skills/infisical-ui/rules.json) also drive the workbench Rules page. Every rule, shared or component, has a `detect` field: `lint` names a check in `frontend/scripts/check-v4.ts`, `test` names the test that exercises it, and `review` means only a reader of the change will catch a break. Generation fails on a rule without one.

- Primitives are the shadcn Radix set (`radix-nova`), restyled by `v4.css`. Do not add a second primitive library.
- Colors, type, radius and motion timing (`--v4-duration-*`, `--v4-ease-*`) come from `tokens.json`. Square corners are canonical (`--corners: 0`). The soft scale is an available mode: `V4Scope corners="soft"` sets `data-corners="soft"`, which turns the multiplier to 1. Always multiply a radius token by `var(--corners)`. Do not hard-code hex, raw Tailwind palette classes, a fixed radius, or a literal duration or easing.
- The workbench uses a sidebar brand header, a wide Human preview article, readable Agent measure and responsive comparison cards, with floating Human/Agent and theme controls. Brand tokens define its type, color and radius.
- Brand neon lime is `--v4-accent`, paired with `--v4-on-accent`. The shadcn `bg-accent` role is neutral selection/hover, not brand lime. Primary (and default, its alias) Buttons are the ink fill for the one main action; only accent Buttons use the shared lime material, for approval and grant moments. Keep the global primary role ink and selection neutral. Follow rule/button-material in the canonical rules; do not repaint Buttons in examples.
- Use `V4Scope` for the docs boundary and portal container. Use the existing ThemeProvider for theme changes.
- Orgs have no avatar.
- After UI edits, run `npm run lint` in `frontend/`. Also run `npm run lint:v4` and `npm run ui:lint`. `ui:lint` runs the v4 checks against a baseline that only shrinks: a new finding fails, a fixed one is locked in with `npm run ui:lint -- --update`. Exempt one line with `v4-check-ignore <check> -- <reason>` on it or the line above; the reason is required. `lint:v4` is `@shadcn/lint` (`no-raw-colors`, `no-restyle`) on the docs route. It is not part of `npm run lint`, because loading it there blows the 15 minute CI lint cap. Do not add spacing or type classes to a v4 component. Wrap it instead.
- Add components with `npx shadcn@4.22.0 add <name> -y` from `frontend/`, which reads `components.json`. Do not run `shadcn init` here. It would retarget the app. The CLI resolves aliases from the root `tsconfig.json`, which is a solution file and must not gain a `paths` block: that slows the frontend lint past its 15 minute CI cap. If add cannot resolve `@app/*`, copy the `paths` block from `tsconfig.app.json` for that command only, and do not commit it.
- Primitives import `cn` from the `cn` package. That is the registry's helper. Do not rewrite those imports.
- These unrelated upstream items remain outside this React 18 foundation: attachment, bubble, direction, marker, message, message-scroller, questionnaire, trace.

Read the generated component guides in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md) or run `npm run ui:info -- <name>` from frontend. `npm run ui:generate` refreshes tokens, the catalog, documentation and standard registry payloads; `npm run ui:check` detects stale output and missing contracts. Start `npm run ui:dev` for the backend-free workbench. Verification recipes in metadata are not passing evidence.

## Human examples

Use the shared preview frame and ExampleGrid, ExampleCell and ExampleStage presentation components. Compare supported variants, distinct sizes and applicable states as labeled peers. Captions sit 8px below their own specimen and describe its actual state. Specimens and captions align to the start, and specimens in a row share a bottom baseline, so the captions of a row line up. Equal-appearance aliases share one specimen. Keep specimens in one row of similar height; give a much taller one its own row.

Use only the composition needed to demonstrate the component. Do not add synthetic save/reject/reset controls, request logs, export workflows or stress-test toolbars to Human pages. Ordinary action buttons do not become pressed toggles merely to produce feedback. Keep core interactions working and relevant states visible. Put technical orchestration in component tests and explain constraints in the closed Usage and rules disclosure. Generated Agent examples lower documentation-only presentation wrappers to native layout elements, so they remain portable.

## Icons

Lucide (`lucide-react`) is the icon source of truth for v4. Use `Icon` (52 product names mapped to Lucide, or any Lucide icon through `icon`) or import Lucide directly. `assets/icons-legacy/` holds the original Infisical 2.0 line set from #8691 for reference only: nothing imports it and the registry does not ship it. Do not hand-draw SVG icons.

# Component guide

Generated by ui:generate from the typed family contracts.

- [Access list](access-list.md): Who can reach a project: a member per row that opens them, multiple selection with the bulk bar and a locked owner.
- [Activity log](activity-log.md): Who did what, one line per event, grouped by day with load more.
- [Animated collapse](animated-collapse.md): Reveal a region without leaving hidden descendants in the tab order.
- [Announcements](announcements.md): What's new, as cards that cycle in a 480px dialog with dots, Back and Next.
- [Approval queue](approval-queue.md): Requests waiting on you, each moving through new, pending, then resolved or failed in place.
- [Accordion](accordion.md): Reveal related sections without leaving the current context.
- [Alert](alert.md): Explain a persistent result or problem next to the affected content.
- [Alert Dialog](alert-dialog.md): Confirm an irreversible consequence before performing it.
- [Aspect Ratio](aspect-ratio.md): Keep a media or preview region at a defined width-to-height ratio.
- [Avatar](avatar.md): Identify people and show grouped participants.
- [Badge](badge.md): Show a short status, version or environment beside its object.
- [Breadcrumb](breadcrumb.md): Show the current location and links to its ancestors.
- [Button](button.md): Trigger a named action with a clear emphasis and pending state.
- [Button Group](button-group.md): Join related actions without giving each its own container.
- [Calendar](calendar.md): Choose a date with keyboard-accessible month navigation.
- [Card](card.md): Group one resource or task with its own header, content and actions.
- [Carousel](carousel.md): Browse a finite set of related panels with explicit previous and next controls.
- [Chart](chart.md): Present numeric data with a shared legend and tooltip contract.
- [Checkbox](checkbox.md): Stage an independent choice, including a mixed selection state.
- [Collapsible](collapsible.md): Show optional details from a single trigger.
- [Command](command-menu.md): Find and execute an action using a searchable command list.
- [Context Menu](context-menu.md): Expose secondary actions from a context menu.
- [Dialog](dialog.md): Edit or inspect a task in a modal with a title and description.
- [Drawer](drawer.md): Present a modal panel that opens from a screen edge.
- [Dropdown Menu](dropdown-menu.md): Choose an action or setting from a trigger menu.
- [Empty](empty-state.md): Explain why a collection has no items and how to create one.
- [Field](field.md): Connect a control to its label, description and validation error.
- [Hover Card](hover-card.md): Show supplementary information on hover or keyboard focus.
- [Input](input.md): Enter a single-line value with native input behavior.
- [Input Group](input-group.md): Compose a text input with leading and trailing controls.
- [Input OTP](input-otp.md): Enter a fixed-length verification code in connected slots.
- [Item](item.md): Arrange one object with its title, description, media and actions.
- [Label](label.md): Give a form control a persistent accessible label.
- [Menubar](menubar.md): Group application menus with keyboard navigation.
- [Navigation Menu](navigation-menu.md): Navigate between related destinations and expandable groups.
- [Popover](popover.md): Show a small interactive panel anchored to its trigger.
- [Progress](progress.md): Expose determinate or indeterminate progress with numeric semantics.
- [Radio Group](radio-group.md): Choose one option from a visible group.
- [Resizable](resizable.md): Resize adjacent panels using a separator handle.
- [Scroll Area](scroll-area.md): Scroll constrained content with a styled scrollbar.
- [Select](select.md): Choose one value from a Radix listbox.
- [Separator](separator.md): Separate adjacent groups visually or semantically.
- [Sheet](sheet.md): Inspect or edit a task in a side panel.
- [Skeleton](skeleton.md): Reserve content space while a resource is loading.
- [Slider](slider.md): Choose a numeric value or range from a bounded scale.
- [Sonner](toast.md): Announce a short-lived result through themed toast notifications.
- [Spinner](spinner.md): Show the Infisical pixel mark while real work remains pending.
- [Switch](switch.md): Apply an immediate boolean setting with its own pending and recovery state.
- [Tabs](tabs.md): Switch between peer views in the same context.
- [Textarea](textarea.md): Enter multiline prose with native text editing.
- [Toggle](toggle.md): Turn a single pressed state on or off.
- [Toggle Group](toggle-group.md): Select one or several pressed options in a compact group.
- [Tooltip](tooltip.md): Explain a control on hover and keyboard focus.
- [Code](code.md): Display literal machine text inline or in a scrollable block.
- [Code block](code-block.md): Frame code or redacted JSON with a label, actions and truthful copy feedback.
- [Combobox](combobox.md): Search and choose one option from a provided list.
- [Cover](cover.md): The brand cover: a display title and tagline beside a block composition drawn from the system's tokens.
- [Data grid](data-grid.md): Spreadsheet selection and exact typed edits over stable row identities.
- [File tree](file-tree.md): A named hierarchical file and folder picker with one keyboard tab stop.
- [Floating action bar](floating-action-bar.md): Bulk actions for the current selection, floating over the bottom of the view while anything is selected.
- [Icon](icon.md): Render a Lucide icon by product name or directly, on the shared size and stroke tokens.
- [JSON](json.md): Inspect a JSON tree with recursive redaction before rendering.
- [Keyboard shortcut](kbd.md): Keyboard key caps with platform-aware modifiers and readable sequences.
- [Layout measures](layout.md): Compose responsive layouts with source spacing tokens and shared width measures.
- [List](list.md): Object rows with independent current state, selection and actions.
- [Loader](loader.md): Fill a region with a labeled Spinner while its first data loads, then show the content.
- [Middle truncate](middle-truncate.md): Keep both ends of a long identifier within its available width.
- [Multi-select](multi-select.md): Choose several known options without closing after each selection.
- [Multi step](multi-step.md): A task in steps where each step checks its fields before the next, in a dialog, a sheet or the page.
- [Page header](page-header.md): The top of a page: the page-level trail, the title with its badges, a lede, actions and tabs.
- [Pagination](pagination.md): Page ranges, numbered or compact navigation, and manual load more.
- [Sensitive editor](sensitive-editor.md): Explicit reveal and replacement editing with host-owned access and persistence.
- [Settings card](settings-card.md): One setting, or a few that save together, with a footer that shows status and Save.
- [Sidebar](sidebar.md): The app's navigation beside the inset: tools, sections of rows, footer rows and one account button for the person and their organization.
- [Snippet](snippet.md): Present a selectable one-line command and copy its literal value.
- [Table](table.md): Semantic object tables with a typed data companion for selection and large datasets.
- [Text](text.md): Use shared body and supporting-text measures.
- [Top bar](top-bar.md): The strip across the top of the inset with the product-level breadcrumb on the left and page-wide tools on the right.

# Access list Who can reach a project: a member per row that opens them, multiple selection with the bulk bar and a locked owner. ## Choose this component Choose AccessList for a membership list with bulk changes. Use a Table when people need to sort, filter or export members. ## Usage rules ### access-list-roles Owner: access-list. When a member has a role or temporary access. Do: Name the role in a Badge and say when temporary access ends, such as Read, 1 hour. Avoid: Color-code roles or hide the expiry in a tooltip. Why: Words survive both themes and screen readers; color alone does not. Checked by: review only. Look for: Read each row's badge and description for the role and any expiry. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/patterns/access-list.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/access-list/default.tsx ### access-list-owner Owner: access-list. When a member cannot lose access, such as the owner. Do: Make the row unselectable, disable its menu and say why in the description. Avoid: Let the owner be selected and fail the bulk action. Why: A control that cannot succeed should not be offered. Checked by: review only. Look for: Select all and check the owner stays unselected. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/patterns/access-list.tsx ## State guidance - revoked: Rows leave the list and the footer offers Undo. - empty: A compact empty state says nobody else has access yet. ## Presentation rules Do: Say how each member got access in plain words. Avoid: Show internal policy identifiers as the description. Why: People decide on access by who granted it and why. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/patterns/access-list.tsx - src/components/v4/patterns/patterns.module.css Exports: AccessList. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - A toolbar above the list says how many have access and offers Add member. - Members are link rows in a framed List with selection, an Avatar, the role as a Badge, how they got access, last use and a row menu. - Selecting rows raises a contained FloatingActionBar with Revoke access. The owner cannot be selected and its menu is disabled. - After a revoke, a status line in the list footer says how many lost access and Undo restores them. ## Accessibility - The List's select-all and row checkboxes are named for the member; the bulk bar is a named toolbar with a count status. - Machine and agent names are set in mono. ## Use cases - Use AccessList for who can reach one project or resource, with roles in words and temporary access saying when it ends. ## Avoid - Color roles, or confirm every revoke with a dialog when Undo can restore it. ## Limits - The host owns the members and persists revokes and restores. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. # Accordion Reveal related sections without leaving the current context. ## Choose this component Choose Accordion for several independently useful disclosure sections. Use Collapsible for one optional region and Tabs for peer views. ## Usage rules ### accordion-usage Owner: accordion. When a collapsed section contains invalid fields. Do: Give each heading a distinct content name, reveal invalid content after submission and keep essential task instructions outside collapsed sections. Avoid: Hide the only error explanation behind a closed Advanced panel. Why: People cannot repair a hidden field or complete a task from headings that conceal the instructions most of them need. Checked by: review only. Look for: Submit invalid content inside a closed item; the item opens, its named heading remains locatable and the invalid field can receive focus. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/accordion.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/accordion/default.tsx ## State guidance - single/multiple: Choose single for one open section or multiple when users compare sections. - invalid: Reveal invalid content and move focus to its field after submission. ## Presentation rules Do: Write headings that identify the hidden content. Avoid: Use a stack of identical More details headings. Why: Repeated headings make scanning and keyboard navigation ambiguous. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/accordion.tsx Exports: Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Radix single mode uses a string value; multiple mode uses an array. onValueChange reports item values, and collapsible allows the open single item to close. ## Accessibility - Each trigger is a button inside a heading and controls its own panel. Arrow keys, Home and End move between triggers. ## Use cases - Use stable item values and choose single or multiple mode from whether simultaneous reading is useful; allow long trigger text to wrap. ## Avoid - Encode required form choices in open sections or hide an unresolved validation error only inside a closed panel. ## Limits - Disclosure does not persist a setting or validate its contents; the host owns those operations. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. # Alert Dialog Confirm an irreversible consequence before performing it. ## Choose this component Choose AlertDialog when a specific irreversible consequence needs confirmation. Use Dialog for editable tasks and an inline action for easily reversible work. ## Usage rules ### alert-dialog-usage Owner: alert-dialog. When deleting a named resource requires an asynchronous request. Do: Name the resource and consequence, offer Cancel before submission, and close only after the request succeeds. Keep cancellation available while pending only if the host can actually cancel the operation. Avoid: Use a generic Are you sure prompt whose action closes before the request settles. Why: The user needs the exact consequence and a retry path when the deletion fails. Checked by: review only. Look for: Confirm a failed asynchronous revocation; the dialog and error remain. Cancel works before submission, and pending cancellation is offered only if it actually stops the operation. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/alert-dialog.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/alert-dialog/default.tsx ## State guidance - pending: Control open state and prevent repeated destructive submission. - error: Keep the dialog open with the failed action and recovery text. ## Presentation rules Do: Label the action Delete connection or Revoke access. Avoid: Label both trigger and confirmation Continue. Why: Vague labels hide which irreversible operation is being approved. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/alert-dialog.tsx Exports: AlertDialog, AlertDialogAction, AlertDialogCancel, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogMedia, AlertDialogOverlay, AlertDialogPortal, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogTrigger. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Controlled open/onOpenChange or defaultOpen owns visibility. Action and Cancel are Radix close controls; an async operation must explicitly control closing while it runs. ## Accessibility - Title and Description name the alert dialog. Focus starts on Cancel and returns to the trigger on close. The dialog stays inside the viewport, and Escape inside an open editor closes that editor first. ## Use cases - Control open state or prevent the Action default close, retain the resource and consequence text, and close only after the host confirms success. ## Avoid - Assume AlertDialogAction waits for a promise or close the confirmation before a failure can be shown. ## Limits - Action does not await a request or infer success; prevent its default close or control open while an async operation settles. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. # Alert Explain a persistent result or problem next to the affected content. ## Choose this component Choose Alert for a condition that remains relevant beside the affected content. Use Toast for a recent transient result and AlertDialog before an irreversible action. ## Usage rules ### alert-usage Owner: alert. When a connection remains unavailable after a failed attempt. Do: State which connection failed and offer a retry or recovery action beside the explanation. Avoid: Show a generic Something went wrong banner at the top of an unrelated page. Why: The location and named object explain what the action will repair. Checked by: review only. Look for: Read the notice without its color. It still names the affected connection, current condition and available recovery, with no duplicate result announcement. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/alert.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/alert/default.tsx ### alert-condition-and-recovery Owner: alert. When an inline condition needs an explanation or recovery action. Do: Choose info, ok, warn or bad from the actual condition, name the affected resource and give any recovery action a real handler. Avoid: Use a warning tone for ordinary metadata, repeat the same success in Alert and Toast, or dismiss a blocking condition without another visible explanation. Why: Persistent notices consume attention and must explain a real condition where it can be acted on. Checked by: review only. Look for: Compare the notice with the current task state. Its tone, resource name, action and dismissal policy still make sense after failure and recovery. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/alert.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/alert/default.tsx ## State guidance - error: Keep the condition visible until it clears or the owner dismisses it. - dismissed: Remove the notice only when the owning state records dismissal. ## Presentation rules Do: Use one notice for one actionable condition. Avoid: Stack a success banner, success toast and green badge for one save. Why: Duplicate feedback competes with the task and repeats announcements. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/alert.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/helpers.module.css Exports: Alert, AlertAction, AlertDescription, AlertTitle, Banner. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Alert supports tone and dismissal for inline feedback. Banner represents a standing condition above related content. ## Accessibility - Use readable text with the tone. Dismissal needs a named button and owner-controlled state when the notice can return. ## Use cases - Use a concise inline condition with a supported tone and only the recovery or dismissal actions that the host can perform. ## Limits - Dismissal calls onDismiss; the owner removes or restores the notice and performs any recovery action. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. Generation checks references and completeness, not rendered behavior or API parity. ### variant - default: example `variants`, visible label "default". - destructive: example `variants`, visible label "destructive". ### tone - neutral: example `default`, visible label "neutral". - info: example `default`, visible label "info". - ok: example `default`, visible label "ok". - warn: example `default`, visible label "warn". - bad: example `default`, visible label "bad". ### actions - action: example `variants`, visible label "Review configuration". - dismiss: example `default`, visible label "Connection failed". ### size support - no authored named size: omitted. This family has no authored sm/md/lg size option. Its dimensions follow content or its container; examples preserve that API. ## Executable examples ### Status and recovery Save this example at `src/pages/design-system/examples/alert/default.tsx`; its relative imports are generated for that exact path. # Command Find and execute an action using a searchable command list. ## Choose this component Choose CommandMenu for searching destinations, objects and actions from one keyboard entry point. Use Combobox for selecting a field value. ## Usage rules ### command-menu-truthful-pending Owner: command-menu. When a command returns a promise that can reject. Do: Keep the action named while pending, retain the command on failure and close only after it fulfills. Avoid: Replace failure with a success notification or clear the query before the person can retry. Why: The visible command must report what the local operation actually did. Checked by: review only. Look for: Reject synchronization, retry the same command and confirm local completion follows fulfillment. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/command-menu.tsx ### command-menu-usage Owner: command-menu. When the menu displays a keyboard shortcut for an action. Do: Register that shortcut in the host and route selection to the same named action as the visible item. Avoid: Display a shortcut cap that does nothing or treat typing as a committed action. Why: The menu should make real actions discoverable, not advertise nonexistent bindings. Checked by: review only. Look for: Search by a visible action label and invoke the displayed shortcut. Both activate the same real action; a typed query alone does not execute it. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/command.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/command-menu/default.tsx ## State guidance - empty: Explain that no commands match the query and retain the query. - pending: Keep asynchronous action feedback outside the closed menu when the action continues. ## Presentation rules Do: Group results by a meaningful type such as Pages and Resources. Avoid: Mix unlabeled destructive actions into a list of similarly named destinations. Why: Search results must make the difference between navigation and mutation clear. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/command.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/command-menu.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/picker.module.css Exports: Command, CommandDialog, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList, CommandSeparator, CommandShortcut, CommandMenuItem, CommandMenuGroup, CommandMenuProps, CommandMenu. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Groups rank label matches while keeping group order; pages drill into a nested command set. onQueryChange receives query and page ID; filter=false delegates filtering to the host. - Pending async commands reject duplicate activation, including the link shortcut; actual dialog close clears page, query and feedback before the next session. ## Accessibility - Arrow keys move through commands and skip disabled ones. Escape leaves a nested page before it closes the menu. Mod+Enter opens an enabled link that is not pending in a new tab. ## Use cases - Give commands stable unique ids, keep page groups meaningful and use filter=false only when the host actually supplies filtered results. ## Avoid - Use CommandMenu as a form value picker, show a shortcut that has no binding or treat closing as proof an action succeeded. ## Limits - Async action IDs stay disabled and busy until settlement. # Context Menu Expose secondary actions from a context menu. ## Choose this component Choose ContextMenu for shortcuts on an already discoverable object. Use DropdownMenu when the action entry point must be visible. ## Usage rules ### context-menu-usage Owner: context-menu. When an essential action appears in a right-click menu. Do: Provide the same action through a visible button or menu, and make the context trigger keyboard reachable. Avoid: Make right-click the only way to inspect, copy or restore an object. Why: Touch users and people who do not discover context menus still need the action. Checked by: review only. Look for: Complete the essential object action without right-clicking; the visible alternative and Shift+F10 context route both reach the intended action. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/context-menu.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/context-menu/default.tsx ## State guidance - disabled: Explain why a locked action is unavailable in surrounding object detail. - copy: Announce copied only after the clipboard write fulfills; show a failure if it rejects. ## Presentation rules Do: Name menu actions for the object under the pointer. Avoid: Fill the menu with disabled coming-soon entries. Why: Unavailable placeholders hide the actions a person can use now. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/context-menu.tsx Exports: ContextMenu, ContextMenuCheckboxItem, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuPortal, ContextMenuRadioGroup, ContextMenuRadioItem, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuShortcut, ContextMenuSub, ContextMenuSubContent, ContextMenuSubTrigger, ContextMenuTrigger. # Cover The brand cover: a display title and tagline beside a block composition drawn from the system's tokens. ## Choose this component Choose Cover for brand surfaces. Use PageHeader for product pages. ## Usage rules ### cover-tokens Owner: cover. When the cover art changes. Do: Draw blocks from color, radius and space tokens so theme and corner choices carry through. Avoid: Hard-code colors or corner radii in the SVG. Why: The cover is the system's own sample and must follow its settings. Checked by: review only. Look for: Toggle the theme and check that every block follows it. Why: The composition carries the brand by itself. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/cover.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/cover.module.css Exports: Cover. # Dialog Edit or inspect a task in a modal with a title and description. ## Choose this component Choose Dialog for a focused editable task. Use AlertDialog for irreversible confirmation and Sheet for supporting details kept beside the page. ## Usage rules ### dialog-adverse-content Owner: dialog. When a focused task includes a long history or a rejected form submission. Do: Keep long content inside the viewport and retain the entered draft beside its error. Avoid: Use a short happy-path fixture as the only sizing check or celebrate an unfulfilled save. Why: A modal must preserve the repair path even when content and text enlarge. Checked by: review only. Look for: Open the long history at 320px and 200% text, then reject a changed name and retry without losing the draft. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/dialog.tsx ### dialog-usage Owner: dialog. When saving a modal form can fail. Do: Keep the dialog open while saving, retain the draft on rejection, and place the error beside the form. Avoid: Close on submit and show success before awaiting the result. Why: Closing loses the repair context and can falsely claim persistence. Checked by: review only. Look for: Submit a failing save, correct it and retry. The draft survives failure, the dialog closes only on confirmed completion and focus returns to a logical target. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/dialog.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/dialog/default.tsx ## State guidance - opening: Give the dialog a specific title and an initial focus target. - dirty: Make the host's dismissal policy explicit before a draft is discarded. ## Presentation rules Do: Keep one focused task and its necessary context in the dialog. Avoid: Recreate a full settings page with nested navigation inside a small modal. Why: A crowded modal makes orientation and recovery harder than a page would. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/dialog.tsx Exports: Dialog, DialogClose, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogOverlay, DialogPortal, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - open/onOpenChange or defaultOpen controls the Radix dialog. Trigger and Close compose native controls; scoped Content portals into V4Scope and scrolls within the viewport. ## Accessibility - Title and Description name the dialog. Focus stays inside it and returns to the trigger. Escape inside an open editor closes that editor before the dialog. ## Use cases - Keep a named DialogTitle and useful description, let the task owner manage pending/error/open state and keep the failed draft inside the dialog. ## Avoid - Wrap an async submit in an unconditional close control or remove the only close path without a deliberate pending policy. ## Limits - Dialog does not submit forms, await requests or choose success/error copy; the task owner controls those states and closure. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. # Drawer Present a modal panel that opens from a screen edge. ## Choose this component Choose Drawer for a dismissible edge panel where drag interaction is useful. Use Sheet for a side task without a drag model and Dialog for a centered focused task. ## Usage rules ### drawer-usage Owner: drawer. When a drawer can be dismissed by a gesture. Do: Provide a visible close control and protect a dirty draft through host-controlled open state. Avoid: Make swipe the only exit or connect a drag gesture to irreversible work. Why: Gestures need an equivalent discoverable control and must not silently commit work. Checked by: review only. Look for: Open and close the panel without a swipe, then test a dirty draft. The visible exit works and host dismissal cannot silently lose unsaved input. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/drawer.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/drawer/default.tsx ## State guidance - open: Keep title and dismissal visible within the panel. - pending: Prevent a host operation from being mistaken for a completed action when the drawer closes. ## Presentation rules Do: Use the panel for one supporting task. Avoid: Layer several drawers to imitate page navigation. Why: Stacked edge panels obscure origin, focus and the remaining task. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/drawer.tsx Exports: Drawer, DrawerBody, DrawerClose, DrawerContent, DrawerDescription, DrawerFooter, DrawerHeader, DrawerOverlay, DrawerPortal, DrawerTitle, DrawerTrigger. It forwards a div ref and native props; Content continues to accept arbitrary children. Use one intentional scroll owner. - Drawer forwards Vaul's controlled open/onOpenChange, direction and drag behavior; its Content and Overlay portal into the current V4Scope. ## Accessibility - Provide DrawerTitle and DrawerDescription. Focus stays inside the open drawer and returns to the trigger. Escape inside an open editor closes the editor before the drawer. ## Use cases - Choose direction from the task layout, give the drawer a title and decide whether dismissal is allowed while the host operation is pending. ## Avoid - Use a drag gesture as the only close path or allow a pending task to disappear without a defined draft policy. ## Limits - Drag thresholds and dismissal are Vaul behavior; the host must choose whether a pending task may be dismissed. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. # Dropdown Menu Choose an action or setting from a trigger menu. ## Choose this component Choose DropdownMenu for a short set of actions or checked preferences behind a visible trigger. Use Popover for editable controls and Select for a form value. ## Usage rules ### dropdown-menu-usage Owner: dropdown-menu. When a menu includes a dangerous operation among ordinary actions. Do: Separate the destructive item, name its consequence, and let the host confirm when necessary. Avoid: Put a multi-field form or an unguarded irreversible action in a generic More menu. Why: Menu selection closes quickly and is unsuitable for a draft that needs validation. Checked by: review only. Look for: Use the menu with keyboard only. Action items do what their labels name, checked items reflect owner state and editable tasks use a suitable form surface. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/dropdown-menu/default.tsx ## State guidance - checked: Control checkbox and radio items from actual preference state. - pending: Keep continuing operation feedback outside the menu after it closes. ## Presentation rules Do: Keep the trigger label tied to the object or action set. Avoid: Use several adjacent unlabeled ellipsis buttons for different action sets. Why: Identical hidden menus make the correct action hard to locate. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/menu-content.tsx Exports: DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuCheckboxItem, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuGroup, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuPortal, DropdownMenuRadioGroup, DropdownMenuRadioItem, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuShortcut, DropdownMenuSub, DropdownMenuSubContent, DropdownMenuSubTrigger, DropdownMenuTrigger. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Open menus retain Radix typeahead and directional keys. Shortcut text requires a matching host handler. - Radix Root owns open/onOpenChange. Action items close after onSelect; checkbox/radio changes stay open by default and can opt into closeOnSelect. ## Accessibility - A named trigger opens the menu. Typing a letter jumps to a matching item, arrow keys skip disabled items and focus returns to the trigger on close. Use checkbox or radio items for persistent selection. ## Use cases - Use Item, CheckboxItem and RadioItem for their actual action or value contract, and prevent default dismissal only when continued interaction is needed. ## Avoid - Style ordinary items to look checked, add buttons inside menu items or announce success merely because the menu closed. ## Limits - Menu checked state and action effects are caller-owned; menu dismissal does not mean an operation succeeded. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. # Empty Explain why a collection has no items and how to create one. ## Choose this component Choose EmptyState to explain why a collection has no rows. Use an error notice for a failed request and a loading state while the result is unknown. ## Usage rules ### empty-state-usage Owner: empty-state. When a filtered collection contains no matching rows. Do: Say that no results match and offer Clear filters when it can help. Avoid: Show a first-use Create resource prompt for a failed request or a filtered result. Why: First use, a filtered result and a failed request require different next actions. A polished empty shell cannot establish which cause occurred. Checked by: review only. Look for: Compare initial-empty, filtered-empty, loading and failure content. Each states the established cause and offers only an applicable next action. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/empty.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/empty-state/default.tsx ## State guidance - first-use: Explain what the collection holds and offer the permitted creation action. - no-results: Keep filter context visible and offer a reset rather than implying all data is absent. ## Presentation rules Do: Use the smallest useful explanation and one relevant next action. Avoid: Add a large celebratory illustration and several unrelated calls to action. # JSON

Inspect a JSON tree with recursive redaction before rendering.

## Choose this component

Choose Json for structured inspection and recursive redaction. Use Code for literal source and Input or Textarea for editing.

## Usage rules

### json-usage

Owner: json.

When a nested object can contain sensitive keys.

Do: Apply the redaction predicate recursively before rendering and copying, and pass only JSON-compatible values.

Avoid: Redact the visible tree while copying the original object or assume collapsed nodes are concealed secrets.

Why: Collapsed presentation is not a data boundary; clipboard content must use the same safe source.

Checked by: review only. Look for: Redact a sensitive key nested in objects and arrays, then copy from a bounded preview. Rendered and copied values use the same recursively safe source.

Source evidence:
- src/components/v4/ui/json.tsx
- src/pages/design-system/examples/json/default.tsx

### json-redaction-before-copy

Owner: json.

When structured inspection includes fields that must not be revealed.

Do: Use named-key or predicate redaction before rendering and copying, and distinguish bounded preview limits from the complete safe copy source.

Avoid: Assume collapsed nodes conceal secrets, copy the unredacted input or describe a truncated preview as the entire document.

Why: Collapsed or limited content can still be present in data; redaction must govern both visible and copied values.

Checked by: review only. Look for: Redact nested values, limit preview depth and copy. The copy contains the full safe document, never the hidden original, and invalid input with redaction requested stays fully redacted.

Source evidence:
- src/components/v4/ui/json.tsx
- src/pages/design-system/examples/json/default.tsx

## State guidance

- collapsed: Keep full safe source available for copy even when preview depth is bounded.
- invalid: Treat unparseable input as literal code, or fully redact it when redaction was requested.

## Presentation rules

Do: Use a bounded tree to expose actual structure.

Avoid: Expand enormous objects by default or decorate each primitive as a badge.

Why: Unbounded structure overwhelms inspection and makes important fields harder to find.

- src/components/v4/ui/json.tsx
- src/components/v4/ui/json-model.ts

- Objects and arrays expand independently with two levels initially open.
- Named-key or predicate redaction replaces values before rendering and copying.

- Each node's toggle is a named button that announces whether the node is expanded.
- The tree is a named scroll region.

## Use cases

- Inspect JSON-compatible data with explicit recursive redaction. Preview limits and expansion govern reading, not safe copy completeness.

## Limits

- Only JSON-compatible values are supported. Preview depth and node counts are bounded; Copy retains the full safe source.

# Multi-select Choose several known options without closing after each selection. ## Choose this component Choose MultiSelect for several known values from a searchable list. Use Checkbox for a few visible independent choices and Combobox for one value. ## Usage rules ### multi-select-usage Owner: multi-select. When a selection grants access only after a host operation succeeds. Do: Keep selected option ids as draft state and let the host authorize and persist the result. Avoid: Treat the checked UI as proof of permission or erase the draft after a rejected save. Why: Selection is an input to authorization, not the authorization decision. Checked by: review only. Look for: Search, select-all and uncheck while a disabled option is already selected. Eligible changes preserve protected choices and the resulting draft does not itself grant permission. When several known values include disabled selections or host-created options. Do: Use sm or md, preserve disabled selections and deselect by unchecking. Avoid: Infer granted permissions from chips, rewrite protected values through select-all or show allLabel when enabled options are not all selected. Why: The summary represents supplied choices; it cannot authorize access or rewrite disabled policy values. Checked by: review only. Look for: Select every option with Ctrl or Cmd+A, uncheck each option, change search during creation and choose a single value. Disabled selections survive, callbacks preserve option ordering and stale creation does not alter selection. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/multi-select.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/multi-select/default.tsx ## State guidance - empty: Explain what may be selected without inventing an initial grant. - overflow: Keep the selected count and a way to review selected options when chips no longer fit. ## Presentation rules Do: Use labels that distinguish each selectable resource. Avoid: Render dozens of full-width chips before the input and hide the search field below them. Why: Selected-value display must leave room to continue selecting. Do: Show empty, protected and long-value cases, and keep creation and permission results owned by the host. Avoid: Treat a checked draft as authorization or drop policy-required choices through a quick action. Why: The input gathers values; it cannot grant permission or certify that persistence succeeded. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/multi-select.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/picker.module.css - src/components/v4/lib/use-option-creation.ts Exports: MultiSelect. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - Multiple and single selection; controlled or local value and open state. Multiple callbacks follow the options order; duplicate option values are rejected at the public boundary. - Default triggers are ordinary fields: the visible purpose comes from a Field label, size defaults to sm32 and explicit md is 36px. label names the trigger for assistive technology and is not drawn inside it. Multiple summaries show the first label and a remaining count, or a caller-supplied allLabel when every enabled option is selected. - Grouping, and a search row that appears only when searchable is set (it is off by default). Selection happens on the options: uncheck an option to deselect it, there is no Clear action. Ctrl or Cmd+A toggles every enabled option and preserves disabled selections. # Pagination Page ranges, numbered or compact navigation, and manual load more. ## Choose this component Choose Pagination for a bounded result set with known pages or explicit load-more progress. Look for: Reject the next page, confirm 10 rows remain, retry and confirm 20 rows only after fulfillment. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/pagination.tsx ### pagination-usage Owner: pagination. When the owner provides onLoadMore for a remote collection. Do: Update host page or progress state after successful loading and pass loading while the request is pending. Avoid: Assume a supplied callback automatically advances controlled page state or reuse stale counts after failure. Why: The host owns fetching and the component cannot infer that new rows arrived. Checked by: review only. Look for: Reject remote loading and then succeed. Current page/progress changes only with actual host results; boundary controls and loaded/total counts remain truthful. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/pagination.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/pagination/default.tsx ### pagination-known-quantity Owner: pagination. When a result collection exposes pages or explicit load-more progress. Do: Choose numbered, compact or more from known data, supply total only when measured and reset the controlled page when page size changes. Avoid: Invent a record total from pageCount, imply infinite fetching or leave the host page unchanged after a successful onLoadMore. Why: Navigation labels must describe actual results and progress rather than inferred quantities. Checked by: review only. Look for: Change page size, load another batch and reach empty data. Controlled state updates, ranges are truthful and pageCount-only usage never invents a total. # Sensitive editor Explicit reveal and replacement editing with host-owned access and persistence. ## Choose this component Choose SensitiveEditor when a stored secret should be fetched only after explicit reveal. Use SecretInput only when the host already permits plaintext in memory. ## Usage rules ### sensitive-editor-usage Owner: sensitive-editor. When a person may replace a stored value without permission to reveal it. Do: Keep stored identity separate from an empty replacement draft and let Save await the host callback. Look for: Replace without reveal, reject a save, change stored revision and reject clipboard permission. No fetch occurs for replacement, the draft survives failure and old plaintext remasks. When a stored secret can be revealed, replaced or copied under changing permission. Do: Keep stored id and revision current, offer only permitted callbacks and preserve replacement without retrieval; await actual clipboard and save promises. Avoid: Pass stored plaintext just to draw a mask, reveal while starting replacement or promise clipboard expiry or reliable memory erasure. Why: Masking is presentation, while retrieval, persistence and permission are host responsibilities with separate lifecycles. Checked by: review only. Look for: Change revision during reveal, reject replacement and retry, then copy with a rejected writer. Stale plaintext does not reappear, the draft survives failure and success follows actual settlement. Source evidence: - src/components/v4/ui/sensitive-editor.tsx - src/pages/design-system/examples/sensitive-editor/lifecycle.tsx ## State guidance - revealed: Remask on Escape and on stored identity or value changes; let the host enforce permissions. - save-error: Keep the replacement draft and error until retry or explicit cancellation. ## Presentation rules Do: Distinguish the stored value from a replacement draft. Show pending work and keep rejection beside the retry action. Avoid: Render a fake masked string as the editable value, announce a save before its promise resolves or claim masking is authorization. Why: A mask is presentation; confusing it with actual data can overwrite or expose the wrong value. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/sensitive-editor.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/data.module.css Exports: SensitiveEditor, SecretInput, CopyButton, StoredSecret. One-line sensitive hosts use 32px with 24px nested reveal/copy actions; multiline content may grow. - Host reveal/save promises receive AbortSignal. Identity/revision change invalidates pending work and clears plaintext. - Copy awaits the actual write before success notification. Failures preserve current draft and show recovery. Why: The account and theme already live in the Sidebar account popover. ## Import and exports - src/components/v4/ui/top-bar.tsx - src/components/v4/ui/top-bar.module.css Exports: TopBar, AppShell, AppInset, PageGutter. Source TypeScript defines the API. ## Behavior - TopBar is 48px tall on a line-soft rule and the inset ground, and sticks to the top of the inset while the page scrolls. - Each crumb with a menu is a switcher segment: clicking its text or its chevron opens the same Switcher, and only the chevron highlights. - AppInset defines one page gutter from its own width. TopBar and PageGutter both pad by it, so the root crumb's text and the page content share a left edge at every width. - Long crumb labels truncate and keep their full text in the switcher. ## Accessibility - The trail is a named breadcrumb landmark. Each switcher's chevron is the only tab stop for its crumb and is named for its purpose and the current value. - AppInset renders the main landmark. ## Use cases - Use TopBar inside AppInset with the organization as the root crumb, then the project and environment, each a switcher, and three or four tools on the right. ## Avoid - Pad the bar or the page by hand, add an organization avatar to the root crumb, or repeat the page-level trail here. ## Limits - The reference's staged narrow-width rules (hiding the search label and ancestor labels) are not implemented; labels truncate instead. - The gutter grows past 40px only when the inset is wider than the page measure plus the gutters. ## Declared example coverage Source declarations and review criteria only. name: infisical-ui
description: Build or review the incubating Infisical v4 foundation, its workbench examples and agent guidance. Use for components, tokens, theming and design-system documentation, not product migration.
---

# Infisical UI

Start with [the v4 instructions](../../AGENTS.md), then query the affected task and read the relevant [canonical rules](rules.json). Always preserve the protected-content boundary. The workbench's Rules page reads that same file. Each rule's `detect` field says who catches a break: `lint` (enforced by `npm run ui:lint`), `test` (a named test) or `review` (a reader of the change).

## Work in order

1. Confirm the boundary. v4 is incubating and fenced from product imports. Keep product code on v3 unless a separate migration is authorized.
2. Run `npm run ui:info -- <task or component>` from frontend. Read the matching generated guide in `src/components/v4/docs/`, then actual exported props and `/design-system#<canonical-id>`. The catalog covers 78 families, including composed patterns and text/layout helpers. Family count and coverage declarations do not prove behavior or visual consistency.
3. Read `tokens.json` for source roles and `v4.css` for current runtime mappings. Do not assume the source specification and every installed primitive already match.
4. Compose the supported Radix API under React 18. Use variants and sizes before classes. On a v4 component, caller classes carry layout only. Raise missing behavior instead of inventing props or adding another implementation.
5. Verify the actual result. Typecheck and run the affected runtime tests, then lint. Use the browser for both themes, narrow layouts, long content, keyboard navigation and open portals. Report checks you did not run.

## Keep the identity

Use warm neutrals, Archivo, Geist Mono and square corners. The soft corner scale is an available mode (`V4Scope corners="soft"`); every radius goes through `var(--corners)` so both modes hold. Primary (and default, its alias) Buttons are the ink fill for the one main action; accent Buttons use the shared lime material for approval and grant moments only. The global primary role remains ink; do not recolor other components to match the Button. The brand neon lime is `--v4-accent` with `--v4-on-accent`; shadcn's `bg-accent` is a neutral hover/selection role. Do not swap them. For brand text or icons, the source `accent-fg` role is exposed as `--v4-accent-fg`. Do not use the light neon fill as light-theme text.

Icons come from Lucide (`lucide-react`), the source of truth. Use `Icon` with a product name or a Lucide icon, or import a Lucide icon directly; stroke follows `stroke-icon` (1.7) and size the size tokens. The original 2.0 line set in `assets/icons-legacy/` is a legacy artifact: never import it or hand-draw SVG icons.

Use `V4Scope` for the workbench boundary so portals inherit its colors, fonts and corner mode. Pass the host's resolved light/dark theme to `V4Scope`, or inherit the nearest host theme. Keep preference and storage in the host. The workbench uses its existing ThemeProvider; installed consumers use their own provider. Do not theme `document.body` or maintain a second preference state.

Protect code, commands, identifiers, protocol payloads, legal and license text, quoted material and user-entered values from prose editing. Never include real secrets in examples, logs or captures. The rules file defines the narrow exemption boundary.

## Checks

These commands belong to this repository. Run from `frontend/`:

```sh
npm run ui:check
npm run type:check
npm test
npm run lint
npm run lint:v4
```

Installed consumers receive the namespaced guidance and readable `docs/README.md`, `docs/components.json` and per-family Markdown. They do not receive this repository's npm scripts or workbench route. Read those shipped files and run the consumer's own build, tests and browser checks.

The stylesheet and runtime regressions cover specific utility, ref, state, progress, portal, focus and theme behaviors. They do not prove all visual rules, accessibility states or component APIs. Copy, hierarchy, rendered contrast and missing coverage still require review.

When adding a primitive, use the existing `components.json` and registry workflow. Do not run `shadcn init`. Check its React compatibility, required packages, support files and installation in a clean consumer before claiming it is installable. A registry JSON build alone is insufficient.

Start `npm run ui:dev` for a backend-free workbench. Human view renders real component examples. Agent view shows the exact generated per-family Markdown, including the compiled example source. Use `npm run ui:generate` after changing tokens, contracts or source dependencies, then `npm run ui:check`. Keep generated coverage separate from executed runtime, browser and clean-consumer evidence.

## Author guidance from evidence

Read the component decision before choosing a primitive. Its rules have a condition, a specific Do/Avoid pair, a reason, source-module evidence and a `detect` field. Generation checks the editorial shape, source ownership and that every `lint` rule and check in `scripts/check-v4.ts` name each other. It also fails when a shared rule's instruction, good or avoid line opens with a lowercase fragment, and when one family's guidance says the same sentence twice. A `review` rule is enforced only by whoever reads the change, so say so rather than calling it verified.

Keep design research outside shipped component source, comments and guidance. Retain primary standards and API references where they support a factual contract. Aesthetic taste is a project decision, not an accessibility claim. Apply a recommendation only when it fits the actual task and exported API. The pinned identity, exact-value contracts and protected-content boundary remain authoritative. Do not create a second policy file that competes with these contracts and rules.

Before publishing an example, inspect its actual narrow and wide rendering. Keep product labels, helper text, synthetic-data disclosure and truthful state feedback inside the specimen. Put inspection instructions in the guide. A control must perform its advertised operation; a click notification must not claim a save, test or reversal that did not happen.

A success message or toast alone does not prove the operation. Verify the changed resource or local model, or compare the exact exported or copied bytes. Bind every shortcut advertised as an available task action in its active context. Check that it invokes the action and respects typing, pending and disabled states where applicable. Explicitly labeled notation, platform, literal-plus and sequence specimens may demonstrate key syntax without registering commands. Keep those specimens distinct from available action hints; do not add meaningless handlers to make a notation comparison appear functional. Record the concrete scenario checked and any remaining limits.

## Author complete examples

Show supported variants and distinct sizes as labeled peers with the same content. Identify equal-size aliases once. Keep applicable states visible beside the default. Use the shared preview frame and labeled comparison cells. Demonstrate pending and failure directly where the API supports them. Keep meaningful component interactions working, and verify complex host orchestration in component tests. Use the actual exported component and its supported props. Do not invent size APIs, empty headings or every combination of independent props. Keep inspection coaching in Usage and rules, outside the specimen. Do not add save/reject/reset simulators, test-control toolbars or unrelated mini-apps to Human examples. Captions follow the specimen and reflect its actual state. Ordinary action buttons must not invent pressed-toggle behavior.

For data-bearing examples, use adverse synthetic content: long names, unbroken identifiers, missing values and zero, one or dense collections where applicable. Pair long text with its neighboring actions. Preserve exact copied and edited payloads. Verify the actual open overlay, focus return and recovery at wide and narrow widths in both themes, including text enlargement where it matters. Record not-applicable cases and unrun checks.

Declare each finite coverage choice against its executable example and visible label, or give a specific omission reason. Generation checks declaration and reference completeness. Source review checks parity with the exported API; browser evidence checks rendering and interaction. None substitutes for the others. Assessment labels describe work to perform, not a result already measured.

Use clear wording or separate text and layout instead of decorative dot separators in authored labels and prose. Preserve literal values, semantic list markers and supported status-dot or Chart dot APIs under the protected-content boundary.

## Keep component relationships consistent

Read the actual type and control recipes before changing measurements. The ordinary control height is 32px with the shared 14px text role. Keep explicit 36px and 40px sizes available. Their nested action boxes are 24, 28 and 32px, accounting for the host border and inset. Button default/sm are aliases; Input/InputGroup/Snippet default to sm. MultiSelect is 32px at sm and 36px at md. Standalone icon aliases are separate recipes.

A type role owns family, size, line height, weight and tracking together. Read the complete title, row-title, field-label, body, helper and technical-value roles from the source. Use the 28/32 page title for ordinary titles and the explicit 44/44 display role only when its scale is needed. Do not reconstruct a role from font size alone.

A control size also owns border-inclusive height, insets, icon box, label gap and any nested action slot. Keep component internals in their owner. Use Stack, Inline, Grid and measures for relationships between siblings. A caller padding or font patch hides a missing shared recipe and will drift in the next composition.

Compare filled and outlined actions beside fields using the same supported size. Compare nested Copy, Reveal and Clear independently from standalone icon actions. Adding an action must not enlarge a one-line host or erase the distinction between its advertised sizes. Check a pending label and long content in the same comparison. Equal outer boxes still need optical review for their text baseline and visual weight.

Keep ordinary sections open and quiet. Frame data, code or a distinct task when its boundary helps. The frame does not choose title rank. Equivalent titles keep the same role in Card, settings and plain sections, and their named header, body and footer slots own the shared content edges. Titles, counts, metadata and actions need separate slots rather than concatenated strings.

Use content-driven rows for lists and one effective uniform metric where virtualization requires it. Table and DataGrid rowHeight values are requested minimums; enlarged content can raise the shared effective height used by rendering, virtual slices and navigation. They do not support arbitrary variable-height rows. Compare the actual compiled row height with the scroll model, including nested controls and borders. A height declaration that loses to a child's minimum size is not a working virtual-row contract. Preserve row ids through reordering and keep current details separate from bulk selection.

## Write rules that change an author's decision

Start with the closest alternative. Explain why this task needs a searchable field value, pressed tool, peer panel, action menu or sequential workflow. Then read the supported props and coverage omissions. Describe the real variants and sizes without inventing another dimension to fill a comparison. A family with no named size should say so. An alias is one measurement with two supported names, not another visual size.

Use a condition that can occur in this component. Give the supported construction, the concrete mistake and its consequence. Name an assessment that could disprove the claim. For example, a virtual-row rule compares actual row height with the supplied metric while scrolling across slices. It does not merely assert that the source contains a height token. A copy rule checks the exact safe payload after fulfillment and rejection; a green toast alone proves neither.

Preserve existing specific rules that cover a different risk. Refine overlapping prose instead of adding a quota of rules or repeating the global bans in every family. Authored assessment instructions remain instructions until a recorded test or review executes them. Keep source, behavior, rendered review and clean installation evidence separate.

Human mode shows variants, supported sizes and meaningful states first. Put usage, states, accessibility, rules and anti-slop decisions together in its one initially closed Usage and rules disclosure, written as what the person sees and decides. Keep behavior, limits, API tables, source and verification instructions in Agent mode. Required help, permission reasons, synthetic-data disclosures and actual errors remain visible beside the relevant control. Remove coaching sentences that narrate what a person should click merely to inspect an example.
